αὐτὸν τὸν ψωμὸν ἔχει τις ἕνα, κἂν μὴ ἔχῃ ἄρτον ὁλόκληρον, ἀφαιροῦμεν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ,
λέγοντες· ἀλλ' ὀφείλεις. Ταῦτα οὖν λέγει, ἐγκαλῶν τῷ Ἰὼβ, ὅτι ἀμφίασιν γυμνῶν
ἀφεῖλεν. ζʹ–θʹ. Οὐδὲ ὕδωρ διψῶντας ἐπότισας, ἀλλὰ πεινώντων ἐστέρησας ψωμόν·
Ἐθαύμασας δέ τινων πρόσωπον, ᾤκισας δὲ τοὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Χήρας δὲ ἐξαπέστειλας
κενὰς, ὀρφα νοὺς δὲ ἐκάκωσας. Οὐκοῦν οὐ μόνον τὸ ἀδικεῖν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ μὴ
εὐεργετεῖν ὑπεύθυνον· ἐπισημαίνει δὲ μέχρι τοσούτου εὐεργεσίας ἐκτείνειν ὀφεί
λομεν, ὅποτε ὑπεύθυνον τὸ μὴ ποτίσαι δι ψῶντας. Ὥσπερ οὖν διὰ τὸ ποτήριον
ψυχροῦ ὕδατος μισθὸν λαμβάνομεν, πολλὴν μέντοι ἀπηνίαν τοῦ Ἰὼβ
καταψηφίζεται, ὡς μηδὲ ὕδωρ τὴν ἀδάπανον χάριν παρέχοντος, καὶ τὸ μεῖζον
κακὸν, τῷ διψῶντι. Ἀλλὰ πεινώντων ἐστέρησας ψωμόν. Τί λέγω, φησὶν, ὅτι οὐ
παρέσχες τῷ δεο μένῳ; ὅποτε καὶ τὴν μικρὰν παραμυθίαν τοῦ ἄρτου παρὰ τοῦ
πεινῶντος ἀφείλου· ψωμὸν γὰρ λέγει τὸ τμῆμα τοῦ ἄρτου, ὥσπερ καὶ ἐν τῇ Ῥοὺθ
κεῖται· Βάψαι τὸν ψωμόν σου ἐν τῷ ὄξει. Ἐθαύμασας δέ τινων πρόσωπον. Τουτέστι
καὶ τὰς κρίσεις οὐ δικαίως, οὐδὲ ἀπαθῶς, ἀλλ' ἀνθρωποπαρέσκως ἐποίησας,
προσωπολήπτης γὰρ γέγονας· καὶ δικάζων οὓς μὲν ἐξῇρες, οὓς δὲ ἐταπείνους, τοὺς
μὲν ταπεινοὺς βιαζόμενος, τοὺς δὲ ἐν δυναστεί αις θαυμάζων καὶ τιμῶν. Ὤικισας δὲ
τοὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Τινὰ δὲ τῶν ἀντιγράφων ἀντὶ τοῦ ᾤκισας ἐκοίμησας ἔχει· ἵνα εἴπῃ
καὶ αὐτὴν τῶν πτωχῶν τὴν στρωμνὴν ἀφείλου, ὡς ἐπὶ τοῦ 372 ἐδάφους αὐτοὺς ἐξ
ἀνάγκης κοιμᾶσθαι, μη δὲν ἔχοντας ὑπεστορεσμένον ... Χήρας δὲ ἐξαπέστειλας. Ἢ
τῶν προσόντων αὐτὰς ἐγύμνωσας, ἢ μᾶλλον προσελθούσαις καὶ ἐλεημοσύνην ζη
τούσαις οὐδὲν δέδωκας, ἀλλ' ἀπεπέμψω μη δὲν λαβούσας ἀπὸ σοῦ ... Ὀρφανοὺς δὲ
ἐκάκωσας. Τὸ δὲ τοὺς ὀρφανοὺς καὶ ἀβοηθήτους κα κοῦν, ἐσχάτης κακίας γνώρισμα.
Οὐδένα μὲν γὰρ δεῖ κακοῦν, ἐξαιρέτως δὲ χρὴ φείδεσθαι τῶν ὀρφανῶν· περὶ γὰρ τῶν
ἀβοηθήτων ψυ χῶν πολεμεῖν ὁ Θεὸς ἐνετείλατο. Πλέον δὲ παρὰ τοὺς ἄλλους
ἀνθρώπους, πτωχοὶ, χῆ ραι, ὀρφανοὶ δέονται βοηθείας. ιηʹ. Βουλὴ δὲ ἀσεβῶν πόῤῥω
ἀπ' αὐτοῦ. Ἰδόντες δίκαιοι ἐγέλασαν. Ἃ οἱ ἀσεβεῖς βουλεύονται, πόῤῥω ἐστὶν ἀπὸ
τοῦ Θεοῦ. Ἰδόντες [δίκαιοι] τὴν βουλὴν τῶν ἀσεβῶν, κατεγέλασαν αὐτούς. κβʹ.
Ἔκβαλε δὲ ἐκ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐξη γορίαν, καὶ ἀνάλαβε τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ ἐν καρδίᾳ
σου. Τὴν ἐξηγορίαν ἐζήτουν κατ' ἐμαυτὸν, τί σημαίνει; Καὶ εὗρον ἐν ἄλλῃ ἐκδόσει,
παρὰ τῷ Συμμάχῳ, ἀντ' αὐτῆς, τὴν ἐξομολόγη σιν. Παρὰ δὲ τῷ Ἀκύλᾳ· Νόμον. Φησὶν
οὖν κατὰ μὲν τὸν ἕνα· Ἐξομολόγησαι περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων σου· τὸν δὲ τρόπον τῆς
ἐξη γορίας παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ διδάχθητι. Κατὰ δὲ τὸν ἕτερον· ∆έξαι παρὰ Θεοῦ νόμον,
καὶ τοὺς λόγους αὐτοῦ ἐγκαρδίους ποίησαι. Εἰ δίκαιος εἶ καὶ ἄξιος, ὑπαγορεύθητι
παρὰ Θεοῦ, καὶ δέξαι θεῖα ῥήματα ἐξ σῇ καρδίᾳ, ὡς ὕστερον Ἱερεμίας ἤκουσεν· Ἰδοὺ
δέδωκα τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὸ στόμα σου. Ἢ ἐξηγορίαν τὴν ἐξο μολόγησίν φησιν,
προτρέπων εἰς μετάνοιαν τὸν δίκαιον. Ἢ τοῦτο λέγει, ὅτι μετάβαλε τὸν τρόπον, καὶ
ἀνάλαβε τοὺς θείους νόμους. 373 Ἢ ὅτι ἐξαγόρευσον τὰ ἡμαρτημένα σοι, καὶ τοῦ
λοιποῦ τοὺς λόγους τοῦ Θεοῦ φύλαττε. Τῆς διπλῆς δὲ ταύτης ἐννοίας ἐκεῖθεν ἔσχον
τὰς ἀφορμὰς, τὴν ἐξηγορίαν. κδʹ. Θήσῃ ἐπὶ χώματι ἐν πέτρᾳ, καὶ ὡς πέτρα χειμάῤῥου
Σωφείρ. Βαλεῖς εἰς γῆν, καὶ οἱονεὶ κακώσεις αὐτόν. Κεφ. ΚΓʹ, βʹ. Καὶ δὴ οἶδα ὅτι ἐκ
χειρός μου ἡ ἔλεγξίς ἐστιν, καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ βα ρεῖα γέγονεν ἐπ' ἐμῷ στεναγμῷ.
Τουτέστι τὸν κατήγορον μετ' ἐμαυτοῦ περιφέρω, τὸν ἔλεγχον, τὴν ἀπόδειξιν τῶν
κακῶν οἴκοθεν ἔχω. –Οἶδα, φησὶν, ὅτι ἐκ τῶν ἐν χερσὶ, τουτέστιν ἐκ τῆς πληγῆς, καὶ
οὐκ ἀφ' ὧν ἔπραξα, δοκεῖτε τοὺς ἐλέγχους ἐπάγειν· καὶ γὰρ βαρέως ἐπέθετό μοι
Θεὸς, ὥστε με στενάζειν. –Οἶδα, φησὶν, ὅτι ἐκ τῶν πράξεων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, αἱ
κρίσεις αὐ τοῖς· πλὴν ὑπὲρ τὴν ἰσχύν μου ἐπετέθη μοι, ἤτοι ἔξω τῆς πράξεώς μου, ὁ
ἔλεγχος. ʹ. Καὶ ἐν πολλῇ ἰσχύϊ ἐπελεύσεταί μοι, εἶτα ἐν ἀπειλῇ μοι οὐ χρήσεται. Καὶ
γὰρ εἰ ἐν πολλῇ ἰσχύϊ χρήσεται μοι καὶ ἀπειλῇ, ἀλλ' ὅμως οἶδα ὅτι ἀλήθεια παρ'
αὐτῷ ἐστιν. ζʹ. Ἀλήθεια γὰρ καὶ ἔλεγχος παρ' αὐτοῦ· ἐξαγάγοι δὲ εἰς τέλος τὸ κρίμα
μου. Τοῦτο ηὔξατο, τοῦτό ἐστιν ὅ φησιν, ὥστε πέρας ἐπιτεθῆναί μου τοῖς δεινοῖς·
εἶτα, φη σὶν, ὅτι ταῦτα ἤθελον γενέσθαι, ὥστε ἀπο θανεῖν, οὐχ ὡς νῦν μέλλοντος
αὐτοῦ κρίνειν. –Παρ' Ἑβραίοις, τὸ τέλος καὶ ἡ νίκη διὰ μιᾶς σημαίνεται λέξεως. ιʹ.
Οἶδεν γὰρ ἤδη ὁδόν μου. Οἶδε, φησὶ, τὴν ὁδόν μου, καὶ ὅτι ἐσπού δασα ἀεὶ ὑπακούειν
pass_a_gloss: (Continues the previous section:) ... the very morsel someone has, a single one, and even if he does not have a whole loaf, we take it away from him, saying: but you owe. These things then he says, accusing Job, that he took away the covering of naked men. Verses 7 to 9. Not even water did you give the thirsty to drink, but you robbed the hungry of a morsel. And you marveled at the face of some, and you settled those upon the earth. And widows you sent off empty, and orphans you did harm to. Therefore not only the wronging, but also the not doing good, is answerable; and he marks that we ought to stretch beneficence up to so much, when it is answerable not to give drink to thirsty ones. Just as then through the cup of cold water we receive a wage, he however votes against Job much harshness, as not furnishing even water, the costless favor, and the greater evil, to the thirsting one. But you robbed the hungry of a morsel. What do I say, he says, that you did not furnish to the one in need? when even the small consolation of bread you took away from the hungry one; for morsel he calls the cut piece of the bread, as also in Ruth it lies: Dip your morsel in the vinegar. And you marveled at the face of some. That is, the judgements too you made not justly, nor without passion, but man-pleasingly, for you have become a receiver of faces; and judging, some you lifted up, and others you humbled, forcing the humble, and marveling at and honoring those in power. And you settled those upon the earth. Some of the copies instead of 'you settled' have 'you put to sleep'; so that he may say, also the very bedding of the poor you took away, so that from necessity they sleep upon the floor, having nothing spread underneath ... And widows you sent off. Either you stripped them of the things belonging to them, or rather, to them coming and seeking alms you have given nothing, but you dismissed them having received nothing from you ... And orphans you did harm to. To do harm to the orphans and helpless is a token of the last wickedness. For one must harm nobody, but exceptionally one ought to spare the orphans; for God commanded to make war about the helpless souls. And more beyond the other people the poor, widows, orphans need help. Verse 18. And the counsel of impious men far from him. Having seen, righteous men laughed. What the impious plan is far from God. Having seen the counsel of the impious, [righteous men] laughed them down. Verse 22. Take (printed 'Ἔκβαλε', cast out; read 'ἔκλαβε', take) out of his mouth a declaration, and take up his words in your heart. The declaration I was seeking by myself: what does it signify? And I found in another edition, in Symmachus, in its place the confession. And in Aquila: law. He says then according to the one: confess about your sins, and be taught from God the manner of the declaration. And according to the other: receive from God law, and make his words in-hearted. If you are righteous and worthy, be dictated to from God, and receive divine words in (printed 'ἐξ') your heart, as later Jeremiah heard: Look, I have given my words into your mouth. Or declaration he calls the confession, turning the righteous man toward repentance. Or he says this, that change your manner, and take up the divine laws. Or that tell out the things sinned by you, and for the rest guard the words of God. And of this double notion I had the occasions from there, the declaration. Verse 24. You will put upon a heap of earth in rock, and as a rock of the winter-torrent Sopheir. You will throw into earth, and as it were you will do it harm. Chapter 23, verse 2. And indeed I know that from my hand is the reproof, and his hand has become heavy upon my groaning. That is, I carry around the accuser with myself, the reproof; the showing of the evils I have from home. I know, he says, that from the things in hands, that is, from the blow, and not from what I did, you seem to bring on the reproofs; for indeed God set himself on me heavily, so that I groan. I know, he says, that from the deeds of men are the judgements for them; except that beyond my strength, or outside my deed, the reproof was laid on me. Verse 6 (label printed 'ʹ' alone; the stigma is lost). And in much strength he will come upon me, then in threat he will not use me. For even if in much strength he will use me and threat, yet all the same I know that truth is beside him. Verse 7. For truth and reproof from him; and may he lead out my judgement to an end. This he prayed, this is what he says, so that a limit be put on my terrible things; then, he says, that I was wanting these things to happen, so as to die, not as him now being about to judge. Among Hebrews, the end and the victory are signified through one word. Verse 10. For he knows already my way. He knows, he says, my way, and that I was eager always to obey (runs on into the next unit)
pass_b_english: … someone has just that one morsel, and though he has no whole loaf, we take it from him, saying: But you owe. So he says these things in charging Job with having stripped the naked of their clothing.

“You did not give water to the thirsty to drink, but deprived the hungry of a morsel. You admired the face of some, and you lodged those who are on the ground. You sent widows away empty, and you ill-treated orphans” (Job 22:7-9). So not only doing wrong but also failing to do good is liable to account. And he points out how far we ought to extend our kindness, since not giving drink to the thirsty is liable to account. Just as we receive a reward for the cup of cold water (Matthew 10:42), so he condemns Job for great harshness, as one who did not give even water, a kindness that costs nothing, and, the greater evil, to someone thirsty.

“But you deprived the hungry of a morsel.” Why do I say, he says, that you did not give to the one in need, when you even took from the hungry man the small comfort of bread? For by “morsel” he means a piece of bread, as it stands also in Ruth: “Dip your morsel in the vinegar” (Ruth 2:14).

“You admired the face of some.” That is, you also gave your judgements not justly, nor without passion, but to please men, for you became a respecter of persons. In judging, you raised some up and brought others low, doing violence to the lowly and admiring and honoring those in power.

“And you lodged those who are on the ground.” Some of the copies have “you laid to sleep” instead of “you lodged,” meaning: you took away even the very bedding of the poor, so that they had to sleep on the floor, with nothing spread beneath them … “You sent widows away.” Either you stripped them of what they had, or rather, when they came to you asking for alms, you gave them nothing but sent them away without anything from you … “You ill-treated orphans.” To ill-treat orphans and the helpless is the mark of the utmost wickedness. For one must ill-treat no one, but above all one must spare orphans, since God commanded us to fight for helpless souls. More than other people, the poor, widows and orphans need help.

“And the counsel of the ungodly is far from him. The righteous saw it and laughed” (Job 22:18-19). What the ungodly plan is far from God. The righteous, seeing the counsel of the ungodly, laughed them to scorn.

“Receive a declaration from his mouth, and take up his words in your heart” (Job 22:22). I was asking myself what “declaration” means, and I found that in another edition, that of Symmachus, “confession” stands in its place, and in Aquila “law.” So according to the one he says: Confess your sins, and be taught by God the manner of the declaration. According to the other: Receive law from God, and take his words into your heart. If you are righteous and worthy, let God dictate to you, and receive divine words in your heart, as Jeremiah later heard: “Behold, I have given my words into your mouth” (Jeremiah 1:9). Or by “declaration” he means confession, urging the righteous man to repentance. Or he is saying: Change your way of life and take up the divine laws. Or: Declare the sins you have committed, and from now on keep the words of God. The starting points for this double sense I took from there, from the word “declaration.”
“You will lay it on a mound in the rock, and like the rock of the torrent of Sophir” (Job 22:24). You will throw it to the ground and, as it were, ill-treat it.

“And indeed I know that the reproof comes from my own hand, and his hand has become heavy upon my groaning” (Job 23:2). That is: I carry my accuser about with me; the reproof, the proof of my evils, I have from my own house. I know, he says, that it is from what is at hand, that is, from the blow, and not from what I have done, that you think to bring your reproofs; for God has laid himself on me heavily, so that I groan. I know, he says, that men's judgements come to them from their deeds; but the reproof has been laid on me beyond my strength, that is, apart from anything I have done.

“And he will come against me in great strength; then he will not use threats against me” (Job 23:6). For even if he deals with me in great strength and threat, still I know that truth is with him. “For truth and reproof are from him; and may he bring my judgement to its end” (Job 23:7). This was his prayer; this is what he means: that an end be set to my troubles. Then, he says: I wished these things to happen, so that I might die, not as though he were now about to judge. Among the Hebrews, “end” and “victory” are expressed by one word.
“For he already knows my way” (Job 23:10). He knows my way, he says, and that I have always been eager to obey …

choices.choice: The old English ended at the Job 22:22 note; Job 22:24, 23:2, 23:6, 23:7, 23:10 and their comments are now translated, plus dropped clauses in 22:7-9 ('and, the greater evil, to someone thirsty', 'Why do I say, he says ...').

'a mere spectator of appearances' -> 'a respecter of persons' (προσωπολήπτης); 'The one who casts a curse from his mouth urges others' -> the Job 22:22 lemma; 'They sought redemption in me' -> 'I was asking myself what declaration means' (ἐζήτουν κατ' ἐμαυτόν); 'Redemption' for ἐξηγορία -> 'declaration'; 'Akylas' -> Aquila; 'one is proclaimed by God' -> 'let God dictate to you'.
'Ἔκβαλε' (cast out) read as ἔκλαβε 'receive', the LXX wording of Job 22:22 and the sense of the comment 'Δέξαι παρὰ Θεοῦ νόμον'. 'ἐξ σῇ καρδίᾳ' read as ἐν σῇ καρδίᾳ.
'ζʹ–θʹ' Job 22:7-9; 'ιηʹ' covers 22:18 and the first words of 22:19 (cited 22:18-19); bare 'ʹ' before 'Καὶ ἐν πολλῇ ἰσχύϊ' is ϛʹ (Job 23:6).

Job 22:24 'You will lay it': θήσῃ has no object, 'it' supplied; 'ill-treat it' for κακώσεις αὐτόν (masculine; referent unclear, perhaps wealth). Matthew 10:42 sentence is an anacoluthon (ὥσπερ ... μέντοι); rendered 'Just as ... so'.

'εἶτα, φησὶν, ὅτι ταῦτα ἤθελον γενέσθαι, ὥστε ἀποθανεῖν, οὐχ ὡς νῦν μέλλοντος αὐτοῦ κρίνειν' rendered closely; meaning unclear. 'ᾤκισας' rendered 'lodged' (οἰκίζω) to keep the contrast with the variant 'laid to sleep'.
